native_result.query: In the PCA conducted on forms of capital, analyzed in hundred-year time slices, how are the symbolic capital components such as house size, daggers, and hatchets/swords characterized in terms of their values on the first principal component (PC1) and distribution across the second principal component (PC2)?
native_result.HypoA: Symbolic capital components such as house size, the number of daggers, and hatchets/swords are characterized by negative values on the first principal component (PC1) and exhibit a wide distribution of values on the second principal component (PC2). This Principal component analysis (PCA) is on the forms of capital. The values of the individual elements of the forms of capital form the attributes.
native_result.HypoB: The symbolic-capital components split across the two leading PCs: on PC1 (30.3% variance) hatchets/swords (+0.30), daggers (+0.27) and house size (+0.23) all load moderately positive together with the prestige goods copper/gold (+0.41), pottery decoration (+0.38) and depots (+0.34), and against subsistence/utility items (sickles, axes/celts, pottery form, amber), so on the dominant wealth-accumulation axis the symbolic trio is not separated from economic capital; on PC2 (19.5% variance) the trio is heterogeneous — house size (+0.33) is displaced onto the second axis with axes/celts (+0.47), amber (+0.44), monument size (+0.39) and monument count (+0.29), while daggers (+0.07) and hatchets/swords (+0.05) are near zero, remaining defined almost entirely by PC1. Weapons are thus pure indicators of the overall capital gradient, whereas house size additionally tracks an independent settlement/monumentality dimension.
native_result.WorkflowB: Parsed capital.csv with decimal commas, dropped group/color, 12 Z columns as variables over 39 100-year BCE slices (4300–500); standardized columns and ran correlation-matrix PCA (SVD). Repeated on deduplicated unique period rows (37). Robustness: time_series_data.csv *_inter columns averaged into the same 100-year BCE bins (37 slices) and re-run. Reported eigenvalues, variance shares, PC1–PC3 loadings, communalities, score–time correlations, and PC1/PC2 loading correlations between runs. PC1 sign fixed only for reporting (majority-positive sum); signs are arbitrary.
